stage_a.note: Extremely energetic, smiling, and positively engaged throughout the live infomercial style pitch.
Sustained, high-energy excitement while demonstrating the product's features and benefits.
Friendly and approachable demeanor, frequently smiling and engaging directly with the investors.

venture.description: A reusable, scratch-free scrubbing sponge that changes texture based on water temperature.
venture.note: The founder gives a comprehensive live demonstration of the product's capabilities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder demonstrates the Scrub Daddy sponge, showing how its texture changes with water temperature to clean various surfaces.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond expresses amazement at the product demonstration.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement at the product demonstration.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin enthusiastically repeats the product name.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond praises the presentation as a fantastic live infomercial.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert praises the presentation as incredible.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the founder has product samples to hand out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms he has samples for the panel.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks where the product is currently being sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains they are in five local supermarkets and have appeared on QVC three times.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks how the QVC appearances performed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder says QVC went fantastic, with reorders increasing each time.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin notes the business is humming and asks for the total sales figures across all channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states total sales are just over one hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if the product has a patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms one issued patent, two pending, plus trademarks and domain names.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks what the requested investment will be used for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder wants to set up an independent manufacturing facility with automated equipment.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks why the founder needs his own manufacturing facility.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains he is currently constrained by his manufacturer's schedule.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert clarifies if the founder could make more revenue with continuous production.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms, citing QVC demand and his eighteen years of manufacturing experience.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks for the cost to make one sponge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder states the manufacturing cost is about one dollar.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the selling price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder says the price is about two dollars and eighty cents.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies if that is the wholesale price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms it is wholesale and mentions his goal of national retail distribution.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin argues the retail price will be too expensive compared to standard cheap sponges.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder argues the product should be compared to high-end brand name scrubbing pads, not the cheapest options.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert doubts the product will succeed in retail settings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains their custom display shippers communicate the product's value in stores.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond points out that retail end caps are expensive to secure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder agrees that end caps are difficult to get even with money.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert repeats his lack of faith in the retail vision and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark warns that depending entirely on QVC for sales is dangerous.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder claims to have three thousand retail stores lined up.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark doubts the retail expansion and dislikes the single-product focus, deciding to exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder expresses disappointment that Mark is out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori defends QVC, noting its massive sales volume and product rotation strategy.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers one hundred thousand dollars for half the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder suggests Kevin's offer is a starting point for bidding.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder jokes that Kevin is out based on his high equity demand.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond offers fifty thousand dollars for fifteen percent, conditional on Lori providing the rest.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori begins to speak but is interrupted by the commercial break.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori offers one hundred thousand dollars for thirty percent, promising infomercial and retail success.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers one hundred thousand dollars with no equity, asking for a per-unit royalty instead.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond questions why the founder would give up thirty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond drops his condition and offers one hundred fifty thousand dollars for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder asks Lori how she will respond to Daymond's new offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori matches Daymond's equity, offering one hundred thousand dollars for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin argues against giving up equity, emphasizing the value of keeping the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if twenty-five percent equity is worth more than his proposed royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori dismisses Daymond's retail connections.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that his royalty deal allows the founder to keep all equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder asserts he knows how to handle the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori defends Daymond's retail success but asks the founder to listen to her.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokes by pretending the sponge is telling the founder to choose his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder asks the panel to summarize the current offers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert recaps the three standing offers from Daymond, Kevin, and Lori.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori increases her offer to one hundred fifty thousand dollars for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond increases his offer to one hundred seventy-five thousand dollars for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori increases her offer to two hundred thousand dollars for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond exits, stating his goal was just to drive up the price for Lori.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin lowers his royalty ask to stay competitive.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert notes the founder has two remaining offers and asks for a decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori demands an immediate decision on her offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder counters Lori, asking if she will drop her equity stake to twenty percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori accepts the counter-offer of two hundred thousand dollars for twenty percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder accepts Lori's deal.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel and founder celebrate the successful negotiation.

decisions.note: Does not believe in the retail vision.
Concerned about being a one-product company dependent on QVC.
First offer to start the bidding.
Conditional on raising the rest from Lori.

decisions.terms: $100,000 for 0% equity, 50 cents per unit until $100k, then 10 cents per unit
decisions.note: Wants to be a financier without taking equity.
Matches equity percentage of Daymond's offer.
Achieved goal of driving up the price for Lori.

decisions.terms: $100,000 for 0% equity, 25 cents per unit until $100k, then 7.5 cents per unit

decisions.note: Asks Lori to reduce her equity stake.

record.notes: Aaron's pitch is structured like a live infomercial. Commercial break at 6:14, with recap following.
